title: Ethernet Attacks: ARP Spoofing & Poisoning
description: arp-watch: every IP -> MAC binding on the mirror with its vendor, and the classic layer-2 attacks on it.

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict the board to addresses in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16 or a bare IP. Empty = no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary. Applies to the IP an alert or binding is about; the pipeline tiles ignore it.

list.name: mac
list.label: MAC (prefix)
list.description: Restrict the binding tables and Recent Alerts to one MAC -- or a prefix, so 48:a9:8a is every device of that vendor block. Lower or upper case, colon-separated. Filled by clicking a MAC.

list.name: severity
list.label: Severity
list.description: Severity on the Suricata scale, 1 being the most severe: 1 gateway_spoof, 2 arp_poisoning, 3 conflicts/floods/sweeps/mismatches and a takeover, 4 a plain MAC change or a new station. Click a bar in Alerts over Time, a Severity cell, or the Critical & High tile to set it; Alerts in Range puts it back to All.

panels.title: ARP Watch
panels.description: What arp-watch itself says about its input, computed in the service: NO TAP (tzsp0 missing), NO MIRROR (nothing received on the tap for arp_watch.silent_seconds), NO ARP (traffic arrives but carries no ARP -- a mangle/IP-only mirror, a filtered sniffer, or an  TAP, whose fabric answers ARP itself), LEARNING (the first hour after the first-ever start: new-station and MAC-change alerts are held back; spoofing and conflicts are not), WATCHING. NOT RUNNING means no health point in 15 minutes. If this is not WATCHING or LEARNING, an empty board below means nothing.

import "array"
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Same helper as the traffic dashboards: the CIDR box becomes an anchored prefix
// regex, the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage. Prefix lengths other
// than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))
// The MAC box is a prefix, so a whole vendor block (48:a9:8a) works too.
macRe = if "${mac}" == "" then /.*/
    else regexp.compile(v: "^" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: strings.toLower(v: strings.trimSpace(v: "${mac}"))))

seen = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "arp_alert" and r._field == "count")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.severity == "1" or r.severity == "2")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group()
  |> sum()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

union(tables: [seen, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()

panels.title: ARP Alerts over Time by Severity (click a bar to drill down)
panels.description: Stacked count of ARP alerts per bucket. Click a bar and pick "Only this severity" to narrow every alert panel below. The bucket is ~1/96 of the range, floored at the service's 60s window, and labelled with the START of its window, so zooming onto a bar selects the alerts that drew it. Colours are pinned per severity.

panels.title: ARP on the Mirror (packets per bucket)
panels.description: What arp-watch read, by kind. Requests and replies are the normal conversation; gratuitous ARP is a host announcing itself (at boot, after a failover) -- a steady stream of it is a flood; unsolicited replies are answers nobody asked for, which is how arpspoof and its relatives work (one every 2 seconds per victim); probes are RFC 5227 duplicate-address checks. Ignores the CIDR box: it describes the capture. Capture drops are frames the kernel had to discard before this service read them -- if that line is not flat at zero, alerts were missed.

panels.title: Alerts by Type
panels.description: How many of each alert in range (Severity and CIDR boxes apply). One bar colour: the bars encode one magnitude. gateway_spoof (1) and arp_poisoning (2) are attacks; ip_conflict, the floods, sweeps and mismatches (3) need a look; mac_changed (4) and new_station (4) are the network changing.

panels.title: IPs Claimed by More Than One MAC
panels.description: Every address that more than one MAC answered for in range, with the claimants and their vendors. Two MACs in a row here is not yet an attack -- one move is a new DHCP lease, which the service reports as mac_changed (info) -- but an attacker is always here: the poisoned address and the attacker's MAC side by side with the real one. A vendor that does not belong (a laptop's NIC next to your router's) is the quickest tell. Per VLAN: the same address in two VLANs is two hosts.

panels.title: Recent ARP Alerts (click a severity to drill down)
panels.description: The last 100 matching alerts. MAC is the address the alert is about (the impostor, the flooder, the new station); Other MAC is the one it is measured against (the real owner, the previous holder, or for eth_mismatch the Ethernet source). first = bindings
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "first_seen")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: float(v: r._value) * 1000.0}))
  |> keep(columns: cols)
last = bindings
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "packets")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _field: "last_seen", _value: float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000.0}))
  |> keep(columns: cols)

union(tables: [packets, first, last])
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with vendor: if exists r.vendor then r.vendor else ""}))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["ip", "mac", "vendor", "vlan"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["last_seen"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 1000)

panels.title: Devices by Vendor (top 15)
panels.description: Distinct MACs heard in range per vendor (CIDR / MAC boxes apply). "(randomized)" counts locally administered addresses -- phones, laptops and VMs that invent their own, the normal case on Wi-Fi today. A vendor that should not be on this network at all is worth a click in the Station Table's Vendor filter. One colour: the bars encode one magnitude.

targets.query:
import "array"
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Same helper as the traffic dashboards: the CIDR box becomes an anchored prefix
// regex, the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage. Prefix lengths other
// than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))
// The MAC box is a prefix, so a whole vendor block (48:a9:8a) works too.
macRe = if "${mac}" == "" then /.*/
    else regexp.compile(v: "^" + regexp.quoteMeta(v: strings.toLower(v: strings.trimSpace(v: "${mac}"))))

bindings = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "arp_binding")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.mac =~ macRe)

bindings
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "packets")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with vendor: if exists r.vendor then r.vendor else "(no OUI database)"}))
  |> group(columns: ["vendor", "mac"])
  |> first()
  |> group(columns: ["vendor"])
  |> count()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 15)
  |> keep(columns: ["vendor", "_value"])
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "devices"})

panels.title: OUI Database
panels.description: Age of the local copy of the IEEE MAC registry (Wireshark's `manuf`: MA-L, MA-M and MA-S merged). dns-resolver keeps it current by itself, re-downloading it once it is a week old -- the publisher asks for no more than that. NOT LOADED means every vendor column is blank: check `docker compose logs dns-resolver | grep oui`, or set OUI_UPDATE=false and put a file in the `oui` volume by hand on an offline host. Always this host's database, whatever the Site box says -- a MAC's vendor is the same everywhere.

panels.title: Capture Drops
panels.description: ARP frames the kernel dropped before arp-watch read them, in range. Anything but NONE means the service fell behind (an ARP storm) and an alert may be missing. tzsp-decap's own UDP drops -- frames that never reached the tap -- are on the Suricata board's Pipeline Health chart.

targets.query:
import "array"

seen = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "arp_watch" and r._field == "capture_drops")
  |> sum()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

union(tables: [seen, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()

panels.title: Protected Addresses
panels.description: How many addresses only their own MAC may claim: every router in mikrotik.host / mikrotik.<name>.host, plus arp_watch.protected. NONE means gateway spoofing can only show up as an ordinary conflict -- add your gateways to arp_watch.protected (pinned as ip=mac where you can: that also catches a poisoner already active when the service first started).

import "array"

seen = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "arp_watch" and r._field == "protected")
  |> last()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

union(tables: [seen, array.from(rows: [{_value: -1}])])
  |> group()
  |> max()

options.content:
ARP has no authentication: hosts believe the last reply they hear. **Spoofing** is answering for an address that is not yours; **poisoning** is doing it continuously so that traffic flows through you. The real owner keeps answering too, so an attack shows as two MACs *alternating* on one IP -- a single change is just a new lease.

Coverage is the router's sniffer: every broadcast, but unicast replies only on the ports it sniffs. Alerts only -- an ARP sender is forgeable, so nothing is blocked.
